A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same posteriors library and research contributions. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison: Appendices A–F in v1 and A–G in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices D–F report original IMDB experiments, Llama 2 continual-learning results and Llama 3 out-of-distribution detection results.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Appendix G adds Bayesian logistic-regression results comparing posterior approximations and runtimes.

M1.justification: The Laplace, VI, tempered SGMCMC and parallel-chain procedures remain unchanged, including the update equations in Appendix B. The new logistic-regression experiment applies existing methods. Expanded descriptions of supported methods and future K-FAC/SVGD support do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds Bayesian logistic regression on the Pima Indians diabetes dataset, extending coverage to classical inference with eight parameters and 768 observations. The IMDB, PG19 and TQA/English-versus-Samoan scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix G introduces evaluated comparisons against Pyro NUTS and BlackJAX SGHMC, which v1 discussed as software without reporting these comparisons. Comparator membership in the three original experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added logistic-regression protocol specifies 5,000 serial MCMC samples, 8,000 VI iterations, and 5,000 independent parallel SGHMC trajectories of 2,000 iterations. It compares full batches with batch size 32 using KSD and runtime. No changed execution settings are established for the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a check of whether minibatching preserves posterior fidelity: Figures 11–12 compare marginal distributions with the NUTS reference, while Table 3 reports full-batch and minibatch discrepancies. The existing temperature, linearization and serial-versus-parallel analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly specifies averaging the logistic-regression results over 10 random seeds with one standard deviation. The five-seed IMDB and four-seed Llama 3 SGD reporting remain unchanged; this is not evidence of increased repetitions for those experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 11–12 and Table 3 add posterior-fidelity and runtime results. For example, full-batch posteriors SGHMC reports KSD 2.693 ± 0.024 and runtime 14.37 ± 0.31 seconds, versus Pyro NUTS at 2.680 ± 0.001 and 15.38 ± 0.74 seconds. The original experimental results, including Tables 1–2, are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds explicit complexity estimates, including O(bd) diagonal Fisher construction and O(kd) diagonal VI iterations. Section 4.1 newly asserts that every implemented SGMCMC algorithm yields valid SGD at T=0, conflicting with the retained SGNHT exception in Appendix C. The existing equations and derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, numbered contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: a scalable functional PyTorch library, the tempered SGD–SGMCMC connection, Bayesian deep ensembles and demonstrations of Bayesian learning benefits. Appendix G supplies additional support for existing compatibility and inference claims.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.2 add specific limitations concerning native convergence diagnostics, model-aware methods, parallel resources, communication costs and tuning. Appendix G qualifies runtime findings through small-model Python overheads and the parallel-resource assumption. The original cold-posterior and mode-trapping interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Figure 3 corrects the undefined output variable to logits and explicitly unpacks state and auxiliary output. Appendix G documents Pyro composition and the Gaussian KSD kernel. Conversely, Section 5.2 removes v1's disclosure of a constant learning rate and between-episode hyperparameter resets, without establishing that execution changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on K-FAC extensions, convergence diagnostics, Bayesian workflow, NUTS and KSD, while removing Cooper et al. (2023). Section 4 more explicitly distinguishes earlier optimizer-specific connections from its claimed general characterization and deep-ensemble corollary. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds the Supported Methods and Complexities subsection and Appendix G, expands limitations, and locally rewrites the introduction, Section 4 and experiment motivations. It adopts author–year citations and removes acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 11–12 and Table 3, replaces the Figure 3 code image, and changes Figure 7's histogram-axis presentation. The ICLR template changes headers, typography and display placement. Existing experimental plots and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix G adds useful direct validation against other inference libraries, while the complexity discussion, expanded limitations and corrected Figure 3 improve practical guidance. These gains are limited by the benchmark's small scale and conditional parallel timing. They outweigh localized drawbacks: omitted continual-learning settings and the new zero-temperature assertion conflicting with Appendix C.
